intro: An Arkansas-born singer with a plainspoken voice.
story: Iris DeMent, the Arkansas-born singer who began with Infamous Angel on Philo in 1992, played Pickathon in 2006. She has two Grammy nominations for Best Contemporary Folk Album and received the Americana Music Association's Trailblazer Award in 2017, presented by John Prine. Workin' on a World, her seventh album, came out in February 2023, and Rolling Stone called it a stirring political statement. On October 6, 2026 she opened for Big Thief at Red Rocks and joined them and Bill Frisell on songs from Horsepower.
artist_reel_line: She opened for Big Thief at Red Rocks on October 6, 2026.

intro: An Iowa folk singer with a gravel baritone.
story: Greg Brown, the Iowa folk singer born in Ottumwa in 1949, made his first album, The Iowa Waltz, for Red House in 1981 and played Pickathon in 2006, the year The Evening Call came out. He has two Grammy nominations for Best Traditional Folk Album, one for Friend of Mine, shared with Bill Morrissey, and one for Slant 6 Mind. In 2010 he sang the part of Hades on Anais Mitchell's folk opera Hadestown. His last studio album was Hymns to What Is Left in 2012, he stopped touring in 2019 and played two final shows in 2023, and the songbook Ring Around the Moon was published in April 2024.
artist_reel_line: The songbook Ring Around the Moon was published in April 2024.

intro: A founding voice of new acoustic fiddle.
story: Darol Anger, a fiddler who had played with the David Grisman Quintet, was already a founding voice of new acoustic music when he played Pickathon in 2006. Fiddlers 4, with Bruce Molsky, Michael Doucet and Rushad Eggleston, was nominated for the 2003 Grammy for Best Traditional Folk Album. He taught at Berklee, where he is now professor emeritus, received the IBMA Distinguished Achievement Award in 2020, and leads the quartet Mr Sun.
artist_reel_line: The IBMA gave him its Distinguished Achievement Award in 2020.

intro: A zydeco bandleader who took over his father's Red Hot Louisiana Band.
story: C.J. Chenier, born in Port Arthur, Texas, joined his father Clifton Chenier's Red Hot Louisiana Band on saxophone in 1978 and took over leading it after the zydeco king died in December 1987. The band appeared on PBS's Austin City Limits in 1992, and Step It Up! came out in 2001. They played Pickathon in 2006, and later played Jazz Fest in April 2013 and the NPR World Cafe XPoNential Music Festival, a set released in 2014.
artist_reel_line: The band played Jazz Fest in April 2013 and the XPoNential festival in 2014.

intro: A San Francisco old-time banjo band.
story: The Earl Brothers are a San Francisco bluegrass band led by banjo player Robert Earl Davis, with no actual brothers named Earl in it, and they emerged in 2004, the year their debut album was reviewed. They played Pickathon in 2005 and again in 2006. Later records include Whiskey, Women & Death, Outlaw Hillbilly and White Album, their fourth self-produced project.
artist_reel_line: Robert Earl Davis released a new video in October 2026.

intro: A San Francisco old-time string band.
story: The Stairwell Sisters, an all-woman old-time string band from the San Francisco Bay Area, formed in 2003, with Evie Ladin on banjo, Stephanie Prausnitz on fiddle, Lisa Berman, Sue Sandlin and Martha Hawthorne. They cut Feet All Over the Floor in 2005, and roots producer Lloyd Maines recorded the follow-up, Get Off Your Money. They played Pickathon in 2006.
artist_reel_line: Lloyd Maines recorded the follow-up to Feet All Over the Floor.

intro: A Kansas City honky-tonk and string band.
story: The Wilders, a Kansas City honky-tonk and string band that formed in 1999, with fiddler Betse Ellis and Ike Sheldon on guitar and lead vocals, played Minnesota Public Radio's Prairie Home Companion with Iris DeMent in June 2002, the Kennedy Center in 2004 and Woodsongs in 2005. Throw Down came out on Free Dirt Records in 2005, and they played Pickathon in 2006 and returned in 2011, the year of their self-titled record.
artist_reel_line: They returned to Pickathon in 2011, the year of their self-titled record.

story: Juanita Family Band was a Portland country band formed in 2005 by singer Lana Rebel, who also fronted the noise-rock band Last of the Juanitas, as an outlet for the country songs she kept writing. It played Pickathon in 2006.
artist_reel_line: A Portland country band formed by Lana Rebel, who also fronted Last of the Juanitas.

story: Packway Handle Band, an Athens, Georgia bluegrass band formed in 2001, were finalists in the Telluride Bluegrass Band Competition in 2002, 2003 and 2004, and played Pickathon in 2006. They won the Podunk Bluegrass band competition in 2009 and later toured with Kid Rock and Foreigner, a run that ended in September 2015.
artist_reel_line: They won the 2009 Podunk Bluegrass band competition, then toured with Foreigner.

intro: A Winnipeg vocal trio on the rise.
story: The Wailin' Jennys formed in Winnipeg in 2002, when a local music shop brought together three solo acts for a performance. They won the Juno for Roots & Traditional Album of the Year (Group) for 40 Days in 2005 and played Pickathon in 2006, the year Firecracker came out. The album drew a 2007 Juno nomination, and a North American airplay count ranked it the number two folk album of 2006. Bright Morning Stars won them another Juno in 2012. The group is now Ruth Moody, Nicky Mehta and Heather Masse.
artist_reel_line: Bright Morning Stars won them a second Juno in 2012.

story: Little Sue is Susannah Weaver, who moved to Portland in 1992 and became a mainstay of the city's alt-country scene. A reviewer called her second album, Crow, produced by Gregg Williams for Cravedog Records, one of the best country albums of 1999, and she played Pickathon in 1999, 2000, 2001, 2003 and 2006. The Long Goodbye followed in 2002 and Baby Knows Better in 2008. She later opened for Bob Dylan, crowdfunded New Light in 2013 with proceeds going to local groups, and in 2019 released Gold, her seventh album of original songs, the year the Oregon Music Hall of Fame inducted her.
artist_reel_line: The Oregon Music Hall of Fame inducted her in 2019.
